Local resource catalog output/feasibility_reproduction/resources/catalog.json, snapshot 2026-10-27: COMP.FUNDA and COMP.COMPANY are cataloged; no dataset name/path/label matches OSHA, whistleblower, enforcement, or misrepresentation. SEC EDGAR raw and parsed exhibit roots are listed, but were not recursively scanned; catalog metadata is not proof of event-level coverage or a construction route.
changes: Assigned observation window remains the documented 2002–2012 enforcement-action cohort; requested pooled endpoint is 2017. The accepted Table 4 estimator pools action-level cases and has no calendar-year term. No code, source data, or paths were modified because the required later case-level inputs and existing construction route are absent.

Resolved the apparent 2013 date in the prepared file as the last regulatory-proceeding end date, not a later action cohort: regbegdt is the date of first regulatory proceeding (maximum 2012-12-20); regenddt is the last regulatory proceeding date (maximum 2013-05-03). The latter does not support post-2012 new-case counts.
limitations: Blocked at preflight; no scientific launch or fresh estimates were made. The prepared action-level file stops at the documented 2012 cohort. The article describes the underlying SEC/DOJ enforcement universe as 1,133 actions through 2012 and the post-SOX sample as 658 actions; the prepared file contains no later action records.

The data sheet says enforcement records were hand-collected over more than 20 years and describes that dataset as proprietary; OSHA complaints were separately obtained through FOIA, with office responses in 2009–2011. The local catalog contains no OSHA/whistleblower or enforcement-case dataset, and the assigned package has no existing builder for either source. SEC/EDGAR exhibits are cataloged locally, but event coverage and a compatible existing case-matching route are not established; new manual source collection/construction is outside this replay.

Current COMP.FUNDA supports filtered fiscal-year observations for 2013–2017, but these can only supply financial characteristics if new cases exist; they cannot supply enforcement outcomes, event dates, or OSHA/other whistleblower flags. The paper/sample record does not specify the provider of the value-weighted market-adjusted return control, so no vendor was inferred.

The separate SAS companion prepares Compustat firm statistics for Table 2 Panel C and Appendix Table A1 Panel C; it does not construct the action-level estimation sample. Those firm-count comparisons are outside this accepted author_analysis Stata scope.

The prior native stage verified that the Stata source ran on the original input, but its saved aggregate files are Table 3 and Table 5 exports; it does not provide a saved focal Table 4 coefficient for a like-for-like comparison. No extended Table 4 estimate exists.

analyses.label: Author Stata analysis stage; focal Table 4 columns 1–3
analyses.reason: The focal Table 4 models are action-level Poisson pseudo-maximum-likelihood fits for firm penalties, employee penalties, and employee prison months on the 658 post-SOX enforcement actions. Their stored touse_sox screen is based on regenddt after July 30, 2002. The requested extension requires new post-2012 enforcement-action outcomes and matching whistleblower classifications. The only prepared analysis file covers the 1,133-action SEC/DOJ universe through the 2012 cohort. The paper data sheet says those cases were hand-collected and the OSHA records came from FOIA; the named package contains no current OSHA update or existing action/OSHA preparation program. Local Compustat has usable 2013–2017 fiscal-year records, but those are not enforcement cases and cannot create the missing outcomes or whistleblower flags. The blocked disposition also covers the other tables/tests in this same accepted Stata entry point because they all use the same case-level prepared data: Tables 2, 3, 5, A1–A4, related descriptive/group tests, sensitivity regressions, and survival analyses. No new observations were imputed or constructed.
source_evidence: output/samples/records/jar-5b21d99d25c5.json: samples[0] defines the main sample as 658 actions, 2002–2012; cited evidence on pp. 12–15 and 42 identifies the 1,133-action universe, the OSHA FOIA records, hand-collected legal records, and post-SOX cohort; p. 47 reports 658 observations in Table 4.

work/CMSW (2017) JAR Stata Code.do: line 144 defines touse_sox using regenddt after the 2002-07-30 SOX date; lines 267–273 are Table 4 and its three Poisson outcome fits; lines 177–613 show the other included tables and estimator/sensitivity families.

CMSW_WB_final.dta, predecessor input SHA-256 2cb6bddce17b2abe6c6a28f33813c1028d23025439a0e2b9ddd4117abcef7273: aggregate inspection confirms 1,133 unique recid rows and 658 post-SOX rows; regbegdt and regenddt have Stata %td formats; regbegdt maximum 2012-12-20 and regenddt maximum 2013-05-03.

CMSW Datasheet.pdf, predecessor package, pp. 1–2, sections 2 and 5: enforcement data were hand-collected and described as proprietary; OSHA records were obtained by FOIA, with responses from mid-2009 through early 2011; supplied programs are Stata analysis and a SAS Compustat firm-statistics program.

CPST Firms (Post SOX Sample Comparison)_2017-04-19.sas, predecessor package, lines 27–62: reads COMP.FUNDA/COMP.COMPANY for Compustat firm comparison statistics; it does not read or build enforcement or OSHA records.

SEC raw/parsed exhibit directories are cataloged but no event-building route is supplied in the assigned package.
